data.title: Nida poll: Interior Ministry seen facing toughest censure grilling
data.description: The Interior Ministry is expected to face the toughest scrutiny in the coming no-confidence debate, according to a Nida Poll survey, with 45% of the respondents believing the opposition has solid evidence against the 18 targeted cabinet ministers.

data.title: Chinese criminal fugitive arrested in Bangkok
data.description: A 37-year-old man wanted in China for alleged links to a transnational crime syndicate and money laundering has been arrested in Bangkok.

data.title: Agents nab Chinese fugitive
data.description: A 37-year-old man wanted in China over alleged links to a transnational crime syndicate and money laundering has been arrested in Bangkok.

data.title: Probe into jumbo's death
data.description: Natural Resources and Environment Minister Suchart Chomklin has ordered an urgent investigation over the death of a wild elephant suspected of being electrocuted by an electric fence in Loei.

data.title: Nigerians held in drug sting
data.description: Immigration police have arrested two Nigerian men in Bangkok in a cocaine trafficking crackdown, seizing 103 grammes of the drug and equipment allegedly used to dilute it with chalk and baking soda.

data.title: MRTA to review Hat Yai's monorail
data.description: The Mass Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand (MRTA) plans to review Hat Yai's monorail project next year, aiming to update a decade-old study to reflect new conditions and lessons from the 2025 major floods.

data.title: PCD probes Rangsit canal after fish deaths
data.description: The Pollution Control Department (PCD) is investigating pollution in Rangsit canal in Pathum Thani after mass fish deaths and reports of dark, foul-smelling water.

data.title: Economic challenges need global action
data.description: Thailand has called for stronger international cooperation to help economies navigate geopolitical tensions, rising energy costs and technological disruption, arguing that global partnerships must turn investment and innovation into tangible benefits for people and businesses.

data.title: Govt fleshes out energy transition plans
data.description: Thailand plans to accelerate its green transition by reducing energy import dependence, attracting private investment and strengthening climate resilience while creating jobs.

data.title: Rayong sweep uncovers 'unlicensed' karaoke spots
data.description: A raid on four karaoke venues in Rayong found that all were operating without entertainment licences, while two were suspected of concealing prostitution, the Interior Ministry said on Saturday.

data.title: Police trace 'cannabis' sweets
data.description: Police are tracing the source of online-purchased sweets suspected of containing cannabis after three family members, including a two-year-old boy, became seriously ill.

data.title: Pension reform needs good governance
data.description: Pension reforms should protect retirement savings while allowing funds to invest in domestic economies, with sound governance and returns for members remaining the top priorities, forum speakers said.

data.title: IMF helps members tackle 'modern risks'
data.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is updating its Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP) to help member countries protect their financial systems against modern threats, including AI, cyberattacks, rising public debt and geopolitical tensions.

data.title: Ministry eyes illegal dumping
data.description: The Industry Ministry is pushing to establish dedicated recycling industrial estates to manage growing volumes of solar panel and electric vehicle (EV) battery waste, while tightening controls on hazardous industrial waste disposal.

data.title: Police officer and insurgent killed in Narathiwat clash
data.description: One police officer was killed and two paramilitary ranger volunteers injured in a clash with suspected insurgents in Sri Sakhon district of Narathiwat on Saturday. One suspected insurgent was also killed.

data.title: Questions mount over gambling site and MP’s husband
data.description: Former Democrat MP Sirichok Sopha is demanding a deeper investigation into the blocking of the crypto gambling website Shuffle.com and the role played in the business by the husband of Bhumjaithai MP Suchada Zhang Thaensap.

data.title: Chinese fugitive ‘oversaw mule accounts worth B2.5 billion’
data.description: Thai police have arrested a Chinese fugitive in Bangkok for allegedly managing mule accounts that circulated over 500 million yuan and arranging visas for members of transnational criminal gangs.

data.title: Minister apologises over e-harvester price blunder
data.description: Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Suriya Juangroongruangkit has apologised for mistakenly quoting a price of 16 million baht each for electric rice harvesters, insisting the ministry has no plans to buy the machines.

data.title: Academic asks why BMA overlooked flood projects
data.description: A Kasetsart University academic has questioned why Bangkok allocated more than 34 billion baht to flood prevention over two years while omitting six major eastern water-retention projects from its action plans.

data.title: THAI opens compensation site for flood-hit passengers
data.description: Thai Airways International has approved compensation measures for passengers affected by flight delays, cancellations and delayed baggage caused by heavy rain and flooding between Sept 26 and 30.

data.title: Government urged to rethink ‘sin tax’ allocations
data.description: Movendi International has urged Thailand to abandon plans to scrap its earmarked tax system, warning that the move could expose public health policies to political interference and pressure from the alcohol and tobacco industries.

data.title: Promised China trip never booked, 45 students stranded at airport
data.description: An investigation has been ordered after 45 Thai students were stranded at Suvarnabhumi Airport after being promised a field trip to China, only to learn there were no flight tickets for them on the departure date.

data.title: Rights groups decry IMF austerity demand
data.description: Coconut farmer Sombat Chuekrod travelled more than 200 kilometres to join hundreds on the streets of Bangkok on Friday demanding that the International Monetary Fund and World Bank change how they deal with the developing world.

data.title: Flood woes test People’s Party
data.description: The devastating floods that paralysed large parts of Bangkok have revived a familiar but consequential question in Thai politics: What exactly do voters expect from their elected MPs when a crisis strikes?

data.title: Korn urges govt to take action on scams
data.description: Democrat Party deputy leader Korn Chatikavanij has urged the government to step up its fight against scam networks, warning that international cooperation means little without action at home.

data.title: Households in NE economically vulnerable: poll
data.description: The household economy in the northeastern region was "vulnerable" during the third quarter, with no expectations of improvement for the rest of the year, a recent poll found.

data.title: Minister apologises over e-harvester price blunder
data.description: Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Suriya Juangroongruangkit has apologised for mistakenly quoting 16 million baht per electric harvester, insisting the ministry has no plans to buy the machines.

data.title: OECD push requires law reform, say experts
data.description: Thailand needs to upgrade its legal and judicial systems ahead of joining the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), academics say.

data.title: Restarting after Hamas terror
data.description: Ouijai Chaisri was hoping to mark her 44th birthday on Oct 7, 2023, when Hamas launched its attacks on Israel, reshaping the Middle East.
